भगवानले धैर्य धारण गर्ने शक्ति प्रदान गरून्। 🕊️😥🙏💞 एउटै दुर्घटनामा अवधेशले गुमाए श्रीमती, ३ छोरी र २ भाइ! 😭💔 ‘गाडीमा म अटाइनँ, भोलि आउँछु’ भन्दै परिवारलाई बिदा गरेका अवधेशको जीवनमा कहिल्यै नमेटिने बज्रपात परेको छ। छठ पर्व मनाउन काठमाडौंंबाट सर्लाहीस्थित घर फर्किने तयारीमा रहेको अवधेश यादवको परिवारका लागि बिहीबारको यात्रा अन्तिम यात्रा बन्यो। मकवानपुरको भीमफेदी गाउँपालिका–६, चिसापानीगढीमा बिहीबार बिहान काठमाडौंबाट सर्लाही जाँदै गरेको इलेक्ट्रिक हायस दुर्घटनामा परेपछि अवधेशले आफ्नो जीवनका सबैभन्दा प्रिय ६ जना आफन्त गुमाउनुपर्‍यो। गाडीमा ठाउँ नपुगेपछि अवधेश काठमाडौंमै बसेका थिए। उनले श्रीमती पुनम देवी यादव, तीन छोरी अनु, दीक्षा र दीपिका तथा आफ्ना दुई भाइलाई घर जान पठाएका थिए। आफू भने भोलिपल्ट जाने योजनामा थिए। तर बिहानै आएको दुर्घटनाको खबरले उनको संसार नै उजाडियो। दुर्घटनामा उनकी श्रीमती, तीन छोरी र दुई भाइको ज्यान गयो। उनका १४ महिनाका छोरा सुदीपसमेत घाइते भएका छन् र थप उपचारका लागि काठमाडौंको मेडिसिटी अस्पताल पठाइएको छ। अस्पताल परिसरमा भावविह्वल हुँदै अवधेशले भनेका थिए, ‘गाडीमा म नअटाएपछि भोलितिर आउँछु, तिमीहरू जाँदै गर भनेर पठाएको थिएँ।’ उनको यो भनाइले दुर्घटनाले एउटा परिवारमा निम्त्याएको असह्य पीडा झल्काउँछ। अवधेशजी, तपाईंमाथि परेको यो दुःख शब्दमा व्यक्त गर्न सकिँदैन। यो कठिन पीडा सहने साहस मिलोस्। हामी सबैको साथ तपाईंका साथमा छ। 😥🙏 दिवंगत आत्माहरूप्रति हार्दिक श्रद्धाञ्जली। शोकाकुल परिवारजनमा गहिरो समवेदना। 🕊️💔 स्रोत: ABC News Nepal, Nepal News तथा अन्य सञ्चारमाध्यम। One Tragic Accident, Awadhesh Yadav Loses His Wife, Three Daughters and Two Brothers! 😭💔 “There was no room for me in the vehicle. I’ll come tomorrow,” Awadhesh told his family before they left. Little did he know that this would be the last time he would see them together. A heartbreaking tragedy unfolded on Thursday morning when an electric HiAce traveling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi met with a devastating accident at Chisapani Gadhi, Bhimphedi Rural Municipality–6, Makwanpur, Nepal. Awadhesh Yadav had stayed behind because there was no space left in the vehicle. He sent his wife, Punam Devi Yadav, their three daughters, Anu, Diksha and Deepika, and his two brothers ahead, planning to join them the following day. But a tragic accident changed his life forever. He lost his wife, all three daughters and both brothers in the accident. His 14-month-old son, Sudip, was also injured and was referred to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu for further treatment. Speaking emotionally, Awadhesh recalled how he had told his family to go ahead because he would join them the next day. Those few words now carry an unimaginable weight of grief. No words can truly describe the pain of losing six beloved family members in a single tragedy. Awadhesh, may you find the strength to endure this unbearable loss. You are not alone; our thoughts and prayers are with you. 😥🙏 Heartfelt tribute to the departed souls. Deepest condolences to the grieving family. 🕊️💔 Source: Nepali media reports. #MakwanpurAccident #AwadheshYadav #NepalTragedy #HeartbreakingNews #PrayForAwadhesh

This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this.
